skill.name: personwise-create-course
skill.description: Create and manage PersonWise courses from topics, text, documents, and reference images. Review content, visuals, access, and publication through the PersonWise CLI.
skill.summary: Build, review, resume, publish, and query structured PersonWise courses.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: The 127 static alerts are false positives caused by documented commands, Markdown formatting, bounded installer checks, and signed descriptor data. Two semantic risks remain: the skill installs externally hosted binaries without enforced native signatures and executes update commands supplied through remote responses. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: The bootstraps install externally hosted executables without enforcing native platform signatures.
remediation.suggestion: Require valid Authenticode and Apple signatures, verify a signed release manifest independently, and publish reproducible source or auditable binaries.

remediation.issue: Update responses can supply command text for the agent to execute.
remediation.suggestion: Parse update actions as structured data and allow only fixed PersonWise executable paths, subcommands, flags, versions, and release origins.

The substitution reads the operating system and architecture for a closed platform allowlist. No user-controlled text becomes a command.
The substitution reads the operating system for a fixed signature-policy check. It does not evaluate or construct user-controlled shell syntax.
The substitution reads the operating system to choose a standard installation directory. It does not evaluate or construct user-controlled shell syntax.
The substitution passes the quoted installation path through printf and tr to reject control characters. This is validation, not dynamic command execution.
The substitution records the quoted installation directory identity for a later race check. The fixed ls command does not evaluate path content as shell syntax.
The substitution computes a SHA-256 digest of the quoted existing executable. It uses a fixed helper and does not evaluate user-controlled commands.
The substitution creates a private, randomly named work directory under the validated target directory. The quoted path is data, not executable shell text.
The substitution measures the downloaded archive and removes whitespace from the numeric result. Both commands are fixed and the archive path is quoted.
The substitution computes the downloaded archive digest for comparison with a pinned SHA-256 value. No dynamic command name or shell evaluation is present.
The substitution lists archive entries so the installer can enforce an exact three-file manifest before extraction. The archive path is quoted and checksum-verified.
The substitution computes the extracted executable digest and compares it with a pinned value. No user-controlled command construction is present.
The substitution reads the operating system before an optional native-signature check. It does not evaluate user-controlled shell content.
The substitution captures codesign metadata from the quoted candidate for an exact identity comparison. The command pipeline is fixed and limited to local verification.
The substitution rechecks the quoted installation directory identity to detect replacement races. This is a local integrity guard, not reconnaissance.
The substitution rehashes the quoted existing executable before replacement to detect races. The command is fixed and does not interpret path text as code.
The URL targets a fixed HTTPS release path and selects only a hardcoded platform artifact. The installer enforces size, archive, and executable SHA-256 checks before installation.
The script uses the standard XDG user binary directory, falling back to HOME/.local/bin. This is an expected user-scoped install location, not covert file access.
HOME/.local/bin is a conventional user-scoped executable directory. The path is explicit and used only for the approved CLI installation.
The hidden name is a temporary installer workspace created with mktemp and removed by a trap. It does not conceal persistent data or access unrelated files.

semantic_findings.title: Externally Hosted Executable Lacks Native Signature Enforcement
semantic_findings.description: The bootstraps download and install an opaque PersonWise executable. Pinned hashes protect integrity, but native signature enforcement is disabled for the reviewed Windows and macOS release.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both installers explicitly fetch and deploy an executable, and the native signature gates are disabled or conditional. Checksums reduce tampering risk but do not make the binary auditable.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Update Action Is Executed as a Command
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to run the exact action command returned by update responses. It does not require structural parsing or an explicit command allowlist.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions directly require execution of response-provided command text after approval. A compromised service or CLI response could convert this update channel into command execution.

content.value_statement: Building a complete course from mixed materials requires careful structure, review, and state tracking. This skill guides PersonWise creation through reliable checkpoints and verified completion.
actual_capabilities: Creates PersonWise course runs from topics, supplied text, or supported documents.
Builds learner-focused blueprints with outcomes, page structure, narration, visuals, and distribution targets.
Uploads named PDF, PPTX, DOCX, Markdown, and TXT sources through the PersonWise CLI.
Reviews outlines, scripts, images, presenters, and course state at defined checkpoints.
Resumes failed or interrupted runs using fresh state, revisions, and idempotent operations.
Publishes courses, enables link access, submits Topics reviews, and queries course records when authorized.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, an eligible account, and available course credits.
Uses the remote PersonWise service, so creation depends on network access and service availability.
Visual quality review requires an agent that can inspect downloaded review sheets.
The workflow cannot purchase credits, bypass limits, or guarantee Topics approval.

use_cases.title: Convert Training Documents
use_cases.description: Turn approved internal documents into a source-grounded course with structured slides, narration, and private access.

use_cases.title: Develop Expert Lessons
use_cases.description: Create a focused course from a topic, then review teaching progression, factual support, and visual quality.

use_cases.title: Maintain Published Courses
use_cases.description: Resume, refine, repair, query, publish, or share an existing PersonWise course from current service state.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Topic Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private PersonWise course about [topic] for [learner group]. The outcome is [outcome]. Use [number] slides and a [tone] teaching style.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a clear topic and learner outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Build From Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a materials-only PersonWise course from [file paths]. Preserve the source facts, target [learner group], and make the final course private.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use approved local documents as the only factual authority.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Refine
prompt_templates.prompt: Open PersonWise course [project ID]. Review the outline, narration, page text, and images. Apply only objective corrections and preserve slide order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing unpublished course at stable checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Resume and Distribute
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume PersonWise run [run ID] with account [alias]. Reconcile current state, complete pending reviews, enable [private or link] access, and verify playability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Recover an interrupted workflow and complete an authorized distribution target.

output_examples.input: Create a private eight-slide onboarding course from the employee handbook.
output_examples.output: Created the course from the named handbook, reviewed the outline and narration, verified all images, and confirmed private playability. The completion record includes source status, revisions, and project identifiers.

output_examples.input: Resume my product safety course and share it with anyone who has the link.
output_examples.output: Resumed the existing run from current state, completed the remaining review checkpoint, enabled link access, and returned the verified share URL.

output_examples.input: Review the visuals in my unpublished history course.
output: Downloaded ordered review sheets for every slide.
Recorded factual, text, layout, and continuity findings.
Regenerated only the failed slides and rechecked the changed images.

best_practices: State the learner, outcome, source boundary, page count, and access target before creation.
Use only named files and request approval before using agent-discovered local content.
Read fresh run and course state before every mutation and after every interruption.
anti_patterns: Do not interpolate course content into shell commands or expose credentials and signed URLs.
Do not claim completion, publication, or visual quality from queued or partial state.
Do not purchase credits, broaden visibility, or create additional courses without authorization.

faq.question: Which source files are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports named PDF, PPTX, DOCX, Markdown, and TXT files up to the service limit.

faq.question: Can it create a course from a topic only?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create an open-research course from a topic or supplied text.

faq.question: Does it require a PersonWise account?
faq.answer: Yes. Browser OAuth, a compatible PersonWise account, and sufficient course authorization are required.

faq.question: Can it publish or share a course?
faq.answer: Yes. It can publish, enable link access, or submit a Topics review when the user explicitly requests that target.

faq.question: Can it inspect course visuals?
faq.answer: Yes, when the current agent can inspect downloaded review sheets. Otherwise, it records that visual review was not performed.

faq.question: Can it resume an interrupted run?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads current run and course state, preserves identifiers, and continues only through currently allowed actions.
